This is a real asymmetry, NOT a clean iso-clock.

panel.dimension: DIMENSION 2 — IS THE STOP VERDICT CORRECT (vs GREEN)?

findings.claim_checked: (a) rowwise is STRICTLY SLOWER than per-tensor (per-token amax prologue + per-channel scale epilogue vs per-tensor scalar)
findings.problem: The 'strictly slower' direction is sound but the supporting mechanism is only PARTLY load-bearing and one sub-claim is weaker than stated. cipher_rt_fp8_engine.cpp:5-8 confirms per-tensor is a fused cuBLASLt scalar GEMM with NO epilogue and that rowwise is 'NOT_SUPPORTED' on this cu13 cuBLASLt (measured 2026-05-30) — so rowwise must run on a DIFFERENT, less-vendor-tuned path (torch._scaled_mm / CUTLASS), which is the strongest reason it will not be faster. The report's cited mechanism ('per-token amax prologue') is the weak part: per-token amax reads the SAME activation tensor as the global per-tensor amax (same memory traffic), so the prologue is not clearly more expensive; the real extra cost is the per-row x per-col dequant epilogue (M*N, small vs GEMM M*N*K). Net: rowwise<=per-tensor is correct, but it leans more on 'different/less-tuned kernel + lm_head excluded' than on the prologue cost the report names.
findings.evidence: cipher_rt_fp8_engine.cpp:3-8 ('per-tensor scalar ... -> fp16 DIRECTLY (no epilogue)'; 'rowwise NOT_SUPPORTED, measured 2026-05-30'); LANE2_KERNEL_CONTRACT.md:23-26 (rowwise = per-channel W + per-token A via torch._scaled_mm); isoL_fp8_r1.err shows shape #4 m=32000 (lm_head) IS quantized in the per-tensor proxy but the quality contract EXCLUDES lm_head (contract:29), so the per-tensor proxy covers MORE GEMM work => an even more generous upper bound for rowwise.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe the mechanism: the dominant reasons rowwise<=per-tensor are (1) rowwise falls off the fused cuBLASLt path onto a less-tuned scaled_mm/CUTLASS kernel, and (2) quality rowwise leaves lm_head in fp16 (less FP8 coverage than the proxy). Note that even the epilogue cost, while real, is second-order. This makes the bound robust regardless of the prologue argument.

findings.claim_checked: (b)/(d) Confidence 'high' and the value-only option-6 (build rowwise anyway)
findings.problem: The decisive robustness argument is UNDERSTATED, not wrong. The STOP does not actually require 'rowwise strictly slower': even granting the most charitable case where rowwise EQUALS per-tensor speed (zero extra cost), the default-clock (power-relief-included) ceiling is 0.828 < 0.85. So the verdict holds even if the report's (a) claim were entirely refuted. The report frames confidence around three agreeing lines but does not make this stronger 'even-if-equal' point explicit, which is the single cleanest refutation of GREEN.
findings.evidence: phase0_result.json default_clock_fp8_mfu=0.8277 (per-tensor, vendor cuBLASLt fast path, power-relief 1695MHz already included); 0.828 < 0.85 by 2.2 pts; rowwise can only move AWAY from 0.85 (slower), never toward it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence: 'Even in the charitable limit rowwise==per-tensor (zero scaling overhead), default-clock ceiling 0.828<0.85; rowwise being slower only widens the gap.' This makes the STOP independent of the (a) argument.

findings.claim_checked: Mechanism paragraph (lines 65-66): 'Even an infinitely fast FP8 GEMM gives e2e MFU <= V/(1-g) = 0.60/0.354 = 1.69x'
findings.problem: The value 1.69 (with a 'x' multiplier sign) is the asymptotic e2e SPEEDUP ceiling, not an e2e MFU. V/(1-g) = 0.60/0.354 = 1.695 evaluates to a number >1, which is impossible as an MFU (MFU is bounded by 1.0). The same sentence then correctly says 'the asymptote caps e2e speedup at 1.69x', so the prose uses 1.69 as both 'e2e MFU' (wrong) and 'e2e speedup' (right). The conclusion is unaffected — the report acknowledges '-> 1.0 only if g->1', i.e. e2e MFU = V x speedup = 0.60 x 1.69 ~ 1.0 capped at 1.0 — but the mislabel in the load-bearing mechanism paragraph is confusing.
findings.evidence: V/(1-g) with V=0.60, g=0.646 = 1.6949 (computed). An MFU cannot exceed 1.0. The expression V/(g/s + 1-g) as s->inf approaches V/(1-g)=1.69, which is the speedup-times-base, i.e. the speedup ceiling, not an MFU.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'an infinitely fast FP8 GEMM gives e2e speedup <= 1/(1-g) = 1.69x, i.e. e2e MFU -> min(1.0, V*1.69) = 1.0 only as g->1.' Do not call 1.69 an 'e2e MFU'.
